intro: This week's five hottest themes, ranked: a real SCLC signal rescued from a mis-tagged bispecific-ADC fanout, MTAP-deletion synthetic lethality drawing a second sponsor pair, the first Phase 3 win for personalized mRNA cancer vaccines, AI platforms edging into drug design, and a deliberately quiet dealmaking cycle. Refreshed every Monday.

narratives.headline: iza-bren's small-cell readout holds up as a real signal — separate from the six-indication tagging noise around it
narratives.detail: Biokin/BMS's BL-B01D1 (iza-bren), an EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC, threw off six indication tags this cycle from a single NSCLC press item; five checked out as pure mis-tags, but the small-cell occurrence is a genuinely separate signal. A published Phase Ib ES-SCLC dose-expansion readout (NCT05194982) reports a 2L-subgroup ORR of 72.7%, mPFS of 6.2 months, and mOS of 15.0 months — numbers that, if they survive primary-source verification, clear the 2L+ bar set by lurbinectedin (ORR 35%) and tarlatamab (ORR 40%). It is a tidy reminder that genuine multi-indication development and triage over-tagging can look identical until you read the trial.

narratives.headline: A second sponsor pair converges on MTAP-deletion synthetic lethality in pancreatic cancer
narratives.detail: IDEAYA and Genentech opened a clinical collaboration pairing IDE892 (PRMT5 inhibitor) with RG6620 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) in MTAP-deleted, KRAS G12D-mutant PDAC. It sits directly alongside the already-captured vopimetostat-plus-daraxonrasib PDAC readout (92% ORR), which makes MTAP-deletion synthetic lethality a target more than one sponsor is now betting on rather than a single-program idea. No NCT number, phase, or efficacy data has been disclosed for the new combination yet, so the conviction here is about the crowding, not the data.

narratives.headline: Personalized neoantigen mRNA vaccines log their first confirmatory Phase 3 win
narratives.detail: Merck and Moderna's intismeran autogene, an individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccine, delivered the class's first confirmatory Phase 3 result — the modality's most durable signal to date. It resurfaced later in the window only as a duplicate wire pickup, with no new data attached, so this is momentum already banked rather than a fresh readout.

narratives.headline: AI platforms keep arriving at the edge of drug design — two entrants in one cycle
narratives.detail: Two independent signals landed together: a Claude-overseen campaign that designed miniproteins from scratch, and SandboxAQ's AQPotency, a structure-free drug-potency prediction model, launched with Claude/MCP availability built in. Both name the underlying AI infrastructure directly and arrive against the backdrop of the FDA's generative-AI-device discussion paper. Neither carries a clinical or regulatory outcome yet, which is exactly why this stays a watch rather than a result.

narratives.headline: A quiet dealmaking cycle, with Amgen's TScan exit the cleanest move to read
narratives.detail: Amgen exited its T-cell-therapy partnership with TScan Therapeutics, the standout in an otherwise thin roundup that also brushed BioArctic, Enveda, Georgiamune, Kynexis, Tolerance Bio, and Network Bio. Elsewhere, Tolerance Bio and NeoImmuneTech signed a deal worth up to $260M for a thymus-targeting fusion protein entering Phase 2, and Piramal Pharma took a majority stake in Yapan Bio, a Phase I/II vaccines-and-biologics CDMO. None of it touches a clinical asset in the tracked landscape — a quiet week is still worth naming as quiet.
